main_text.p: tur conuiuium: Ac tandem Rebecca cum nutrice", seruo Abrahæ & comitibus eius ad Sponsum abit: qui eam introducit ad tabernaculum Sarę matris, & accipit vxorem, Genes.24.2.&c. Iacob septem annis seruit pro Rachel, &c.29.18.&c. Sichem quum compressisset Dinam, Patrem ablegat ad Iacobum, vt petat nuptias, &c.34.4. &c. Samson ambiens nuptias Dalilæ, re cum parentibus communicata, matrimonium cum ea contrahit, & conuiuium nuptiale agitat, &c.Iudic.14.v.1. &c. Saul per consiliarios agit cum Dauide de nuptiis Filiæ, & dotis loco postulat centum præputia Philisthæorum, 1.Sam.18.25. Dauid ablegat nuncios ad Abigail petitum nuptias eius,25.v.39. 40.41.

MATRIMONIVM inter Sacramenta numeratur à Pontificiis, idque probare nituntur ex epistola ad Ephesios 5. 32. Sed refutantur vel ex epistola ad Colost.1.27. vbi Gentium vocatio dicitur mysterium, vel, vt vetus Interpres vertit, Sacramentum. Vide & Ephes.1.9.& coniugium.

MATTHAEVS, qui & Leui, Publicanus, à Christo vocatur, Matthæi 9.9. Marci 2.14. Lucæ 5.27. conuiuio amplissimo Christum excipit, Matth.9 10. Marci 2.15. Lucæ 5 28. (i. Donatus) fuit Apostolus & Euangelista.
MATTHIAS Discipulus, in loco Iudæ Apostatæ sufficiendus designatur, Actor.1.23.sorte eligitur, versi.26. (i. donum Dei.)
MATHVSALA filius Henoch, Genesis 5.21. nongentos sexaginta nouem annos vixit.v.27. (Methuselah. i. mortis missio.)
MAXILLAM percutienti, altera obuertenda, Matth.5.39. Luc.6.29. maxilla asini occiduntur mille Philisthæi, Iudic.15.15.
IEDAD in castris Mosis prophetat, Num.11.26. (mensurans.)
MEDIATOR, inter Deum & populum Moses, Deut.5.5. (qui internuntius dicitur Gal.3.19. & seruus in domo Dei, & typus Christi.)
MEDIATOR vnus Christus, (Vide CHRISTVS.) 1. Tim.2.5. Heb. 11. 24. per quem & in quo nos D. elegit ab æterno, Eph.14.
MEDICINA à Deo creata, Eccles.38.1.ad 16.vsque V. Prou.68. 15.& Esa.38.21.

page.notes: Faint show-through and a cut-off column strip at the left edge were not transcribed. Several words uncertain in the scan, e.g. "Matth.9 10.", "Iacob septem" and the Greek-free headings; the initial letters of several entries are partly damaged and read as M/I by inference.
